messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: EndoR Clarification
parts:
Hi Mike!

Great work on the new endotherm paper. I was looking through it and noticed that in the discussion you say that the EndoR function still needs to be linked to DEB theory; could you clarify whether that means the function for now is unable to do things like simulate death when the body temperature goes over a critical temperature, allow the animal to hide in a burrow to keep from overheating, things like that?

Best
Adam

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: EndoR Clarification
parts:
Thanks Adam,
But the endoR function certainly allows you to simulated death from heat stress, when a burrow would be needed, etc. You can also work out how much energy and water would be needed for thermoregulation at a snapshot in the organism's life cycle - a 'static energy budget'. The DEB model allows you to simulate the energy budget in terms of growth, development and reproduction over the whole life cycle of the animal. See bioforecasts.science.unimelb.edu.au/app_direct/deb/  We're presently working on integrating it with the endotherm model.
All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: EndoR Clarification
parts:
Hi Adam,
You're not missing anything - you do indeed have to adapt your own code to program in your own behavioural responses. One way to do this is to dynamically vary the behaviour each hour, e.g. by trying different options and choosing the best (e.g. selection of shade and or going under ground). Or, you run a number of scenarios in advance for all time periods and then subsequently process the results to work out what would be the best behavioural option. The latter is more intensive but has the advantage that you could play around with different behavioural priorities and not have to keep running the model other than the initial run.
Hope that helps,
Mike
